claims.text: A Gaussian pulse has σt=0.5. With frequency in cycles/time, σf=1/(2πσt). What is σf? Options: 0.159; 0.318; 0.637. Toy model: compare two controlled cases.

claims.text: For this Gaussian pair, doubling σt changes σf by? The frequency width is inversely proportional to the time width.

claims.text: The Gaussian frequency widths are 0.318 for time width 0.5 and 0.637 for time width 0.25. Halving the time width doubles this frequency width.

claims.text: The product is 1/(2π) under the stated Gaussian and frequency conventions. This is a specific Fourier pair, not an assertion that all pulse shapes have this equality or even finite standard deviations.
